plan.title: KO vs WT drug response: 2x2 interaction DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is an interaction question on a 2x2 factorial design: genotype (WT, KO) x treatment (vehicle, drug), 4 biological replicates per cell, 16 samples, 12,000 genes, raw salmon gene-level counts in counts.csv keyed by gene symbol with the sample table in metadata.csv. The plan therefore fits one DESeq2 negative-binomial model with the design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, with WT and vehicle set explicitly as reference levels, and answers the question from the interaction coefficient (genotypeKO:treatmentdrug) rather than from a comparison of two separately-run analyses. T1S1 first checks sample structure with a blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, a sample-distance heatmap and library sizes, coloured by genotype, treatment and the four-cell condition, so that a mislabelled or outlying sample is caught before it is fitted. T1S2 fits the model, tests the interaction with the Wald test, and also extracts the two simple effects (drug vs vehicle within WT, drug vs vehicle within KO) as named contrasts, each with ashr-shrunken log2 fold changes (ashr rather than apeglm because the KO simple effect is a sum of coefficients, not a single one), BH adjustment within contrast at alpha 0.05, and independent filtering left on. T1S3 assembles the interaction-aware gene table: the two simple effects and the interaction contrast side by side per gene, plus MA and dispersion diagnostics and a p-value histogram. In parallel, T2S1 runs fgsea preranked on the full ranked list of tested genes, once per contrast, using the DESeq2 Wald statistic as the ranking metric (the disputed choice is stated: Wald stat, because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and does not tie at the top the way a saturated signed p-value does), against the human MSigDB hallmark collection with GO BP as the follow-up collection — both are present in the reference store for Homo sapiens. Power is the main caveat and the report must carry it: an interaction coefficient is a difference of differences, its standard error is roughly double that of a simple effect, and at 4 replicates per cell the interaction test is materially less powerful than either simple effect. A gene significant in the KO simple effect but not in WT is NOT evidence of a genotype-dependent drug effect unless the interaction term itself is significant; the report must state that explicitly and must not present the difference-in-significance as the answer.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes
Keep genes with >=10 counts in >=4 samples (smallest group size)
~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment with explicit reference levels WT and vehicle
DESeq2 Wald test on the interaction coefficient plus simple effects, with edgeR quasi-likelihood as the second method
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, within contrast
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, per contrast, MSigDB Hallmark then GO BP
Interaction report: simple effects at WT and KO side by side with the interaction contrast, MA and dispersion plots, reproducibility record

Do not run an over-representation test on the significant-gene list of any contrast if fewer than 50 genes pass padj < 0.05; the ranked test on the full list is the method
caveats: Enrichment on the interaction statistic asks which processes show a genotype-dependent drug response; it is not the same as, and may disagree with, the enrichment of either simple effect. Report the three separately and do not merge the narratives
Enrichment results depend strongly on the method and the collection — present significant sets as hypotheses for follow-up, not as established mechanism
GO BP is a nested hierarchy, so parent and child sets share members and significant hits arrive in correlated blocks; collapse before counting findings
If the interaction contrast has little signal, the ranked test may still return significant sets driven by weak coordinated noise — check the leading-edge gene statistics before believing a set

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on the full tested list, once per contrast, hallmark first for a human dataset (R-0107, R-0048, R-0104). Disputed rule R-0108: the Wald statistic side is chosen and stated. R-0098 names Reactome as the second collection, but no Reactome GMT is staged in this environment, so the staged human GO BP collection takes the follow-up role and the step reports the substitution.

steps.name: Interaction report and reproducibility record
steps.question: Taken together, does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — and with what confidence, given 4 replicates per cell?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. For every gene, present the three quantities side by side: the drug-vs-vehicle effect within WT (the reference genotype), the drug-vs-vehicle effect within KO, and the interaction contrast that is the difference between them — each with its unshrunken log2 fold change, ashr-shrunken log2 fold change, lfcSE and padj, ranked by the shrunken value. Name the reference levels (WT, vehicle) beside the table since every coefficient's meaning depends on them. Carry the MA plot and the dispersion plot as fit diagnostics before the gene tables, plus the per-contrast p-value histograms. Include a volcano for the interaction contrast and per-cell normalized-count plots for the top interaction genes so the four-cell pattern behind each call is visible. State the method, package versions, the design formula, every contrast, the thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering, the number of DE genes per contrast, the gene-set collection names and versions, the ranking metric, the size window and the universe, the random seed, and full sessionInfo. State plainly that FDR is controlled within each contrast and not across the three, that the length offset for salmon input could not be applied because only gene-level counts were supplied, and that a single method (DESeq2) was run — no second-method overlap check is included, so the robustness of individual calls is not established.
steps.context: Depends on the DESeq2 contrasts from T1S2 and the per-contrast enrichment from T2S1. This is the step that answers the research question, and its main job is to keep the answer proportionate to a design with 4 replicates per cell.
acceptance_criteria: A per-gene table giving the WT simple effect, the KO simple effect and the interaction contrast side by side, with unshrunken lfc, shrunken lfc, lfcSE and padj for each, ranked by the shrunken interaction lfc
Reference levels (genotype=WT, treatment=vehicle) stated beside the table
MA plot and dispersion plot presented before the gene tables, each with a sentence saying what it shows
Volcano plot of the interaction contrast, and normalized-count-per-cell plots for the top interaction genes showing all four cells
Explicit statement of the number of genes tested, the number significant per contrast, and the thresholds used
Leading-edge genes of the significant gene sets carried through from T2S1, with the collection, version, ranking metric, universe and size window named
Reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, random seed, gene-set collection version

An explicit power statement: the interaction test at n=4 per cell has low power, and a gene significant in one simple effect but not the other is not evidence of a differential drug effect unless the interaction term is significant
Explicit statement of the two known limitations: FDR is per contrast not across contrasts, and no salmon length offset was applied
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit
Report the interaction contrast and both simple effects together — never the interaction coefficient alone and never a simple effect alone
Do not claim a genotype-dependent drug effect for any gene whose interaction padj is not below 0.05, regardless of how the simple effects differ
Do not describe enrichment hits as established mechanism; frame them as hypotheses and name the method
State the count of untested genes (NA padj from the Cook's outlier flag) alongside the DE counts
caveats: Only one differential-expression method was run, so the recommended two-method overlap robustness check is absent and per-gene calls carry no cross-method corroboration
With 16 samples and no biological replication beyond the 4 per cell, an interaction finding here is a hypothesis for a confirmatory experiment, not a settled result

The tissue is brain: bulk counts are a mixture over cell types, so an apparent interaction can reflect a genotype-dependent shift in cellular composition rather than a change in per-cell regulation. This cannot be distinguished from these data and the report must say so

grounding.reason: Interaction design reporting per R-0092 (simple effects and interaction side by side, reference levels named), shrunken and unshrunken effects per R-0085, MA and dispersion diagnostics per R-0087, method/version/threshold and reproducibility record per R-0041 and R-0086, enrichment provenance and method-dependence caveat per R-0051 and R-0055, leading edge per R-0105. R-0042 (two-method overlap) is not satisfied — only DESeq2 was run, since the knowledge check flagged edgeR QL as not permitted for this interaction situation — so the absent robustness check is declared as a limitation instead.
